issues.description: The template Lecture class defines addGuestStudents with a different parameter list (int, boolean) than the problem statement and the solution, both of which specify addGuestStudents(int). This mismatch will confuse students about the expected signature and will make it harder to follow the UML/specification or to match the reference solution/tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template method signature to match the specification and solution: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) { /* TODO */ }. If validation behavior is desired, either implement it internally or provide an overloaded private helper method; do not require an extra boolean parameter in the public API.

issues.description: The problem statement and the solution expect a method addGuestStudents(int) but the template declares addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput). The extra boolean parameter in the template changes the method signature and parameter expectation, creating a mapping mismatch for students implementing or calling addGuestStudents as specified in the exercise.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template method signature with the problem statement and solution: change the template declaration to public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) and implement any input validation internally (or remove validation parameter). Alternatively, update the problem statement (and solution) to document the additional boolean parameter if that was intended.
